reconcile.connective: The strongest harmonizers treat Genesis 2 not as a rival sequence but as the detailed expansion of the sixth day, so its order poses no objection to Genesis 1.

discrepancy.connective: Julius Wellhausen pressed this as a textbook two-source seam: the Priestly account of Genesis 1 creates humankind 'male and female' together after the animals, while the Yahwist account of Genesis 2 forms the man first, then the animals, then the woman — sequences he held cannot be reconciled as a single narrative.

skeptic.name: Julius Wellhausen
skeptic.work: Prolegomena to the History of Israel
skeptic.attribution: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (Eng. trans. 1885; German Prolegomena zur Geschichte Israels, 1883)

excerpts.excerpt_text: In Gen 1:27 the creation of the woman is linked with that of the man; but here the order of sequence is given, because the creation of the woman formed a chronological incident in the history of the human race, which commences with the creation of Adam. … The circumstance that in Gen 2:19 the formation of the beasts and birds is connected with the creation of Adam by the imperf. c. ו consec., constitutes to objection to the plan of creation given in Gen 1.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly answers the contradiction's core: it concedes Gen 1 links man and woman together yet argues Gen 2 only supplies the 'order of sequence' as a chronological incident, and that the Gen 2:19 animal-formation likewise raises no objection to the Gen 1 plan — the strongest single on-tension harmonization on the row.

pd_work.resource: Keil & Delitzsch, Biblical Commentary on the Old Testament (1861-75), on Genesis 2:18-22
pd_work.author: Keil & Delitzsch
pd_work.note: Treats this exact passage, arguing Genesis 2 gives only the 'order of sequence' and that the Gen 2:19 animal-formation 'constitutes [no] objection to the plan of creation given in Gen 1'; preferred over Haley because its specific-passage coverage is confirmed and it is already surfaced on the row.

link.title: GotQuestions: Why are there two different Creation accounts in Genesis chapters 1-2?
link.note: Live apologetic treatment; argues the two accounts describe one event general-to-specific and reads Gen 2:19 as a pluperfect ('had formed') so the animal order does not conflict with Gen 1.
